uses.quote: In supervised assessments (exams, in-class tests, invigilated practical assessments, vivas, OSCEs), you cannot use GenAI unless your assessment brief expressly allows it.
You can use it to help you prepare/revise: flashcards, quizzes, etc.
In unsupervised assessments (essays, reports, coursework, projects, dissertations, portfolios), you can use GenAI, but you must acknowledge it.
Whatever the assessment, submitting AI-generated content as if it were your own work is academic misconduct.
Asked Gen AI to act like a ‘critical friend’ - questioning her approach and asking her to justify her position

default_when_silent.quote: If your course documentation says nothing about GenAI, this default applies.

decided_by.quote: Your course can set additional limits, and those take precedence – so always read your assessment brief.
course co-ordinators can still indicate, on an assessment-by-assessment basis, any limitations on the use of AI

duty.quote: If you make use of AI at any point in your research or writing process, you must acknowledge the use of that tool as you would any other piece of evidence or material in your submission.

location.quote: When you’ve used Gen AI, you should include a statement to make this clear to your marker.

referencing.quote: You should visit the Library page on referencing styles and select the appropriate style to see what’s appropriate for your work.

consequence.quote: using any form of AI or other computational aids in your university coursework, study, exams, or research without acknowledging that input counts as academic misconduct.
